text:
incident-bot: PAGE: prod-canary-db-migration-failure — SEV2 — @here oncall please. Canary deploy of release/2026-03-15 triggered DB migration that's now blocking requests. See runbook: https://go/redwood/runbooks/db-migration

Samir Patel: I'm oncall — looking now. Which service is timing out?

Maya Park: rollout started 11:02 UTC, canary at 10%. Migration job `add_user_profile_email_index` ran as part of the release. No errors initially, but canary surfaced lots of `500` and long tail latency. Stopping rollout now.

Lina Chen: attaching the error I'm seeing from the migration job:
```
ERROR:  could not obtain lock on relation "users"
DETAIL:  Process 8675309 waits for ShareLock on relation 12345 of database 16384; blocked by process 8675310.
```

Jonas Müller: seeing many backends waiting on a lock, appears migration is trying to create an INDEX CONCURRENTLY but a concurrent transaction is holding an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE? odd. Can you paste output of: `SELECT pid, state, query_start, wait_event_type, wait_event, query FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE state <> 'idle' ORDER BY query_start;`

Lina Chen: pasted short output:
```
 pid  | state  | query_start         | wait_event_type | wait_event | query
------|--------|---------------------|-----------------|------------|-------------------------------
8675309|active | 2026-03-15 11:03:02 | Lock            | relation    | CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY ...
8675310|idle   | 2026-03-15 11:02:58 | Lock            | transaction | UPDATE users SET profile = ...
```

Samir Patel: that UPDATE looks like an app worker doing backfill in-prod — did the release include a code path that backfills on first-read?

Maya Park: yes, the canary toggled feature flag `use_new_profile_index` which lets app write a denormalized profile and trigger a backfill. It should've been off for canary, misconfig happened in the flag rollout. My bad.

incident-bot: Deploy bot: Canary halted for deployment/release-2026-03-15 by Maya Park at 11:05 UTC. Initiating rollback sequence.

Samir Patel: kill-switch the flag now. How to kill quickly?

Maya Park: running kill command in console: `rwctl flags set use_new_profile_index false --force` — done. :white_check_mark:

support-bot: Noting customer impact: between 11:03-11:06 UTC we saw 0.7% of prod requests fail with 500s, 28 unique customers affected, 3 paying customers experienced errors in their sessions. See dashboard: https://go/redwood/monitoring/err-rate

Elena Gomez: CS standby — I'll ping the three accounts and prepare an incident summary to send if we need to escalate.

Jonas Müller: even after disabling the flag migration job process still holds the CREATE INDEX in progress. We need to either cancel the migration backend or kill the blocking transaction. Options: 1) cancel the migration backend (`SELECT pg_cancel_backend(8675309)`), 2) terminate the blocking UPDATE (`SELECT pg_terminate_backend(8675310)`), 3) wait (not acceptable). Any objections?

Lina Chen: canceling the index creation will leave the index state as invalid; we can rollback code path and re-run migration in a safe window. Terminating the blocking backend (8675310) will free the lock faster. I recommend terminate 8675310, then monitor.

Samir Patel: do it.

Lina Chen: executed `SELECT pg_terminate_backend(8675310);` — returned true. CREATE INDEX released, index rolled back to waiting state but DB is responsive again.

ops-bot: rollout-ctrl: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/api-server --to-revision=20260315-3` initiated by Samir Patel at 11:07 UTC. Canary instances are draining.

Maya Park: confirm rollback started, will keep a watch on error rates.

support-bot: Updated affected customers list: 28 customers, 3 high-priority accounts, estimated exposure window 00:03:00. No data loss reported.

Samir Patel: handing off on-call to Jonas for post-rollback monitoring. Jonas, take ownership for next 2 hours.

Jonas Müller: acknowledged — will monitor for 2 hours and start a mitigation PR to remove in-request backfill behavior.

Elena Gomez: preparing customer comms draft now; will hold until we confirm rollback fully stabilized.

Lina Chen: quick root cause summary: feature flag was incorrectly toggled for canary which enabled an in-app backfill that performed UPDATEs on `users` leading to lock contention with a concurrent CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY. The CREATE INDEX could not complete and held locks causing 500s for some API paths.

Samir Patel: immediate action items:
- [x] disable flag (Maya)
- [x] terminate blocker backend (Lina)
- [x] rollback canary (Samir/Ops)
- [ ] open follow-up ticket INCD-3729 for change to flag rollout guardrails (owner: Maya)
- [ ] schedule DB migration window to run index creation in maintenance or use safer online approach (owner: Lina)

Maya Park: will open INCD-3729 now and assign.

incident-bot: Note: timeline saved to incident channel. Please add any postmortem details to the ticket.

Jonas Müller: handing off to oncall rotation at 11:20 UTC — Samir, if anything flares ping me.

Samir Patel: thanks team. Quick blameless postmortem tomorrow 10:00 PT, calendar invite to follow.

Elena Gomez: CS will notify three affected accounts with an explanation and the mitigation steps we took.

Maya Park: follow-up action: add a guard in rollout tooling to prevent enabling write-affecting flags during canary unless explicitly approved.

Lina Chen: note technical mitigation idea: require migration/DDL to be fully decoupled from application rollout and prefer `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` only after traffic is low; also add automated lock detection that aborts risky rollouts.

Samir Patel: closing active page — oncall handoff complete. Will update INCD-3729 with timeline and logs.
